t01.note: A owns the error warmly and personally; B is correct and lean but opens abruptly with 'We are sorry.' and feels colder.

t02.note: A leads with the recommendation and adds reliability and removal cost; B spends words on minute details and off-peak cars.

t03.note: B reads natively (Wasserwerke, Toilettenspülung, proper apology); A has ambiguous 'Spülen', stiff 'Wasserunternehmen' and drops the apology.

t04.note: A's padlock story is consistent and tied to banking; B muddles box versus padlock and has the bank locking with its own key.

t05.note: A keeps frequency, a richer title and a targeted question, though compound; B's question asks what the dashboard already shows.

t06.note: Both keep all five actions; A is tighter, B keeps a little stock closing phrasing.

t07.note: A takes clear ownership with only given facts; B adds a stock 'we know how much you rely' line and less ownership.

t08.note: B explains why sales recovered and what Leeds will do; A is accurate but thinner on causes and the plan's aim.

t09.note: Both correct; A addresses readers directly and keeps 'gesetzlichen Feiertagen'; B leans on passives and 'Anmeldung' for front desk.

t10.note: A gives a vivid simple picture and varied tips; B is more abstract and two of its tips repeat the heat point.

t11.note: A keeps the grit doubt, deadline and options a helper needs; B is clean but drops the time constraint and sanding question.

t12.note: Both keep all five items; A is tighter, B keeps the long greeting and a little extra wording.
